name: Uruguay
headline: Uruguay: +1.8% growth in 2025, 4.7% inflation, debt 66% of GDP
sections: Uruguay is a $85.6 billion economy (2025), the world's 86th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.8% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $38K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 10.0% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.7% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 9.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 7.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 25.1% (2025).
Gross government debt is 66% of GDP (2025), a elevated level. The general government balance is −3.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −0.5% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 50% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 69% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 78.3 years (2024). Population: 3.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
